subsystems.name: Cell source and banking
subsystems.role: provides the starting cells that multiply into muscle and fat.
parts: muscle satellite cells or induced pluripotent stem cells

subsystems.name: Growth medium
subsystems.role: the liquid feed that supplies nutrients and signals for cells to grow.
parts: basal salts, sugars and amino acids

subsystems.name: Scaffold
subsystems.role: an edible or removable matrix that gives a thick cut its shape and texture.
parts: sacrificial moulds that leave channels for nutrients

subsystems.name: Bioprinting and structuring
subsystems.role: places muscle and fat cells in the right geometry and grain.

subsystems.name: Perfusion bioreactor
subsystems.role: keeps oxygen and nutrients flowing to cells buried deep inside the tissue.

subsystems.name: Harvest and finishing
subsystems.role: turns the grown tissue into a safe, saleable cut.

buildSteps.title: Bank the cells
buildSteps.detail: A small biopsy is taken from a live animal; cells are isolated and screened to find lines that divide many times without becoming unstable.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the medium
buildSteps.detail: A serum-free recipe of salts, sugars, amino acids and recombinant growth proteins is made to food-grade purity rather than medicine-grade, since purity level drives most of the cost.

buildSteps.title: Expand the cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells multiply in stirred bioreactors, either floating freely or attached to tiny edible microcarriers, until there are enough for a full cut.

buildSteps.title: Build the scaffold
buildSteps.detail: An edible matrix is moulded or printed with a planned network of channels, because oxygen cannot diffuse through living tissue beyond roughly a couple of hundred micrometres.

buildSteps.title: Seed and print
buildSteps.detail: Muscle and fat cells are combined with the scaffold layer by layer, with fibres aligned so the finished cut has the grain of real meat.

buildSteps.title: Perfuse and mature
buildSteps.detail: Nutrient-rich medium is pumped through the channels for days to weeks; gentle mechanical or electrical stimulation encourages muscle fibres to thicken and firm up.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and finish
buildSteps.detail: The tissue is washed, any inedible scaffold removed, then portioned, textured, and chilled or frozen.

buildSteps.title: Verify safety and scale
buildSteps.detail: Each batch is tested for microbes, allergens and residues, and the same process is repeated at steadily larger volumes to prove it works outside the lab.

prerequisites.tech: Serum-free growth media at food-grade cost
prerequisites.why: the medium is the largest single cost, and pharma-grade growth proteins are far too expensive for a food product.

prerequisites.tech: Edible scaffolds and internal vascular channels
prerequisites.why: without a way to feed cells deep inside, only thin sheets and mince can be grown — not steaks.
existing stirred-tank designs are built for pharmaceuticals: too small, too costly and not suited to structured tissue.
a handful of countries have approved cultivated meat sales since Singapore's first clearance in 2020; most have no framework at all.

prerequisites.tech: Food-safety and labelling rules specific to cultured tissue
prerequisites.why: regulators need agreed tests for allergens, residues and what the product may be called.

pathway.milestone: hybrid products where a small share of cultivated fat or protein is blended into plant-based food
pathway.unlocks: first commercial sales and real cost data at food scale.

pathway.milestone: structured fillets and nuggets grown on edible scaffolds in pilot plants
pathway.unlocks: textures that plant protein alone cannot imitate.

pathway.milestone: whole cuts with marbled fat, produced in perfusion bioreactors of hundreds of litres
pathway.unlocks: steaks and chops at a price premium buyers will pay.

pathway.milestone: commercial-scale plants running on cheap renewable electricity and commodity medium
pathway.unlocks: cost parity with conventional meat for everyday cuts.
